title: Conormal exact sequence of two compatible ring quotients
statement:
Let $\alpha:A\to B$ and $\beta:B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, and assume that $\pi=\beta\circ\alpha:A\to C$ is surjective (hence $\beta$ is surjective). Put $I=\ker\pi$ and $J=\ker\beta$. Give $I/I^2$ and $J/J^2$ their canonical $C$-module structures through $A/I\cong C$ and $B/J\cong C$. For the Kähler differential module and universal derivation of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], there are well-defined $C$-linear maps
$$I/I^2\xrightarrow{u}J/J^2\xrightarrow{v}C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A},\qquad u(a\bmod I^2)=\alpha(a)\bmod J^2,\quad v(b\bmod J^2)=1\otimes\mathrm db.$$
The map $v$ is surjective and $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$. No smoothness, flatness, finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 065V (algebra-lemma-application-NL), with the displayed tensor factors exchanged by the canonical symmetry.

proof.text: Construct the displayed arrows directly. Since $\beta\alpha=\pi$, $\alpha(I)\subseteq J$ and $\alpha(I^2)\subseteq J^2$, so $u$ is well defined. If $c\in C$ is lifted to $a\in A$, then $u(c[x])=[\alpha(a)\alpha(x)]=c\,u([x])$; changing the lift adds an element of $I$ and changes the product by $I^2$. For $b\in J$ put $t(b)=1\otimes\mathrm db$. Additivity and the Leibniz rule give $t(rb)=\beta(r)t(b)$ for $r\in B$, since $\beta(b)=0$. In particular $t(bb')=0$ for $b,b'\in J$, hence $t(J^2)=0$. It therefore descends to the stated $C$-linear $v$. Finally $v(u([a]))=1\otimes\mathrm d\alpha(a)=0$. All tensor equalities here are the balancing relations in the tensor-product definition.

source.place: Tag 065V (lemma-application-NL), the two arrows; Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega) and Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), defining relations.

proof.text: For any $c\in C$ choose $a\in A$ with $\pi(a)=c$; then $\beta(\alpha(a))=c$, proving that $\beta$ is surjective. Apply the surjection-$H_1$ node to $A\twoheadrightarrow C$ and $B\twoheadrightarrow C$. It gives $C$-linear isomorphisms $\theta_A:H_1(L_{C/A})\cong I/I^2$ and $\theta_B:H_1(L_{C/B})\cong J/J^2$. In the canonical presentation $A[C]\to C$, a constant polynomial $a\in I$ lies in the kernel and has zero formal partial derivatives, hence represents a cycle $h_a$. The node's formula, evaluating variables at chosen lifts in $A$, gives $\theta_A(h_a)=[a]$. Likewise each $b\in J$, viewed as a constant polynomial in $B[C]$, defines a cycle $h_b$ with $\theta_B(h_b)=[b]$. As every conormal class has a representative, these describe the inverses of both isomorphisms on every element.

source.place: Tag 07BP (lemma-NL-surjection), applied to both surjections, with its explicit presentation identification from Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy).

proof.text: Use the Jacobi–Zariski node for the given triangle $A\to B\to C$. Denote its map $H_1(L_{C/A})\to H_1(L_{C/B})$ by $q$, and its connecting map by $\partial$. It gives exactness of $H_1(L_{C/A})\xrightarrow q H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow\partial C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$ and of $H_1(L_{C/B})\xrightarrow\partial C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{C/A}$. The same node specifies that $q$ applies $\alpha$ to the coefficients of $A[C]$ and fixes its variables. Consequently $q(h_a)=h_{\alpha(a)}$ for a constant $a\in I$. By step 2, $\theta_B q\theta_A^{-1}([a])=[\alpha(a)]=u([a])$. This proves equality of these maps on all of $I/I^2$, without assuming a naturality result for the conormal identification.

source.place: Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), the middle two exactness assertions and coefficientwise map; Tag 07BP (lemma-NL-surjection).

proof.text: For $b\in J$, use the constant-polynomial cycle $h_b$ of step 2 in the Jacobi–Zariski node's explicit connecting-map formula. The constant polynomial $g=b$ has just its degree-zero coefficient $b$, and the degree-zero monomial evaluates to $1\in C$. That formula therefore yields $\partial(h_b)=1\otimes\mathrm db=v([b])$. Thus $\partial\theta_B^{-1}=v$ on every class of $J/J^2$. This also covers $b=0$ by additivity.

source.place: Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), connecting map in the presentation diagram, with its coefficient formula made explicit in the cited node; Tag 07BP.

proof.text: The surjection-$H_1$ node applied to $A\twoheadrightarrow C$ also states $\Omega_{C/A}=0$. Hence exactness at $C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}$ in step 3 makes $\partial$ surjective, and the isomorphism $\theta_B$ and step 4 make $v$ surjective. For $y\in J/J^2$, set $h=\theta_B^{-1}(y)$. If $v(y)=0$, step 4 gives $\partial(h)=0$; exactness at $H_1(L_{C/B})$ gives $h=q(k)$ for some $k\in H_1(L_{C/A})$. Step 3 then gives $y=u(\theta_A(k))$. Conversely $vu=0$ by step 1. This proves $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$. The only surjectivity hypotheses used were those proved from $\pi$; no flatness or smoothness enters.

source.place: Tag 065V (lemma-application-NL), proof from Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL) and Tag 07BP (lemma-NL-surjection).
